prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t one universal “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, roof type, insurance situation, and whether you value lowest price, fastest scheduling, or the longest warranty. I can’t browse current listings, but I can tell you how to find and vet the best local hail-damage roofers and give you a template you can use when contacting them.

What to look for in a top hail-damage roofer
- Proven hail/insurance-claim experience: contractors who routinely work with insurance companies understand scope descriptions, Xactimate line items, and how to document damage.
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, etc. Certification often gives you enhanced warranties.
- Good reviews and local references: check Google, Yelp/Angi, and the BBB for recent reviews and complaint history.
- Proper insurance and licensing: ask for general liability and worker’s comp certificates. (Colorado has local licensing requirements — check Denver/your county.)
- Written, itemized estimate: includes tear-off vs overlay, materials by brand & class, underlayment, flashing, soffits/vent work, permit fees, cleanup, and warranty terms.
- Permits and inspections: they should obtain required permits and schedule inspections.
- Warranty and workmanship guarantee: written manufacturer and contractor warranties.
- Local/long-running company vs storm-chasers: prefer established local companies over temporary teams that follow storms.

Red flags
- Door-to-door contractors right after a storm who pressure you to sign immediately.
- “We’ll just use your insurance check” or asks you to sign over the check before work is complete.
- Extremely low bids that are vague about materials or scope.
- No physical address, no insurance certificates, poor/zero online presence.

How to choose (step-by-step)
1. Get at least 3 written, itemized estimates (same scope for apples-to-apples).
2. Verify manufacturer certifications and insurance certificates (call the manufacturer or ask to see the contractor’s certification number).
3. Check local reviews and request 2–3 recent local job references you can call or visit.
4. Confirm they will pull permits and handle inspections.
5. Compare warranties and what they cover (labor vs materials, duration).
6. Ask about cleanup and disposal (do they remove old shingles? will they inspect/replace decking?).
7. Use a written contract and require lien waivers on final payment.

Questions to ask each roofer (use when calling or at the estimate)
- How many hail-damage roofs have you repaired in Denver in the last 12 months?
- Are you certified by any shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
- Can you provide proof of liability and worker’s comp insurance?
- Will you handle the insurance paperwork/communication? What’s your process?
- What brand and class of shingles are you proposing? Any optional upgrades?
- Will you obtain permits and schedule inspections?
- What is your warranty (labor) and what manufacturer warranty comes with the shingles?
- Can you provide three recent local references or photos of completed jobs?
- What is your proposed timeline from agreement to completion?

What to do about insurance
- Document damage with photos and video, and request an adjuster visit.
- Bring a roofer to the insurance inspection if possible — an experienced roofer can point out concealed damage.
- Don’t accept a small cash settlement without getting a contractor’s scope first.
- Many quality roofers will work with insurance, but get the scope and price in writing.

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email or text template to request estimates from contractors.
- Create a checklist to take with you to on-site estimates.
- If you give your zip code or neighborhood, I can suggest how to find top-rated roofers near you (search terms and review sources), or—if you prefer—I can list nationally known contractors who operate in Denver (I don’t have live web access, so I can’t fetch current local ratings).

Which would you like me to do next? If you want local recommendations, tell me your zip code or neighborhood and whether you’re filing an insurance claim.
